reason: Chrome sends the RFC 9218 Priority header only on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3. turbo-surf builds request headers before ALPN chooses the protocol and the transport (turbo-surf-wreq) has no per-connection header hook, so it drops Priority only for cleartext origins and for HTTPS origins already known to speak HTTP/1.1. The battery's h1-nav is the cold first request to an HTTP/1.1-only HTTPS origin.

Chrome derives each stream's HEADERS-frame priority from the request priority (weight 256/220/183/147 and an exclusive dependency on the previous stream of the same or higher urgency; transport_identity_chrome156.json). The http2 crate under turbo-surf-wreq takes one connection-level headers_stream_dependency and clears request extensions before the HEADERS frame is built, so a per-request priority cannot reach the frame without forking it. The connection preamble (SETTINGS, WINDOW_UPDATE, pseudo-header order) and the first stream's priority match.

Chrome interleaves page-set (author) headers such as x-battery inside its own order. Author header names are unknowable ahead of time, so wreq appends them after the measured browser order; every browser-owned header keeps Chrome's order.
Chrome's browser UI requests /favicon.ico for every committed document. A browserless engine has no tab strip; emitting the request would need a real UI-driven reason.

Chrome 156 ships V8 15.6.75.19; turbo-surf's stock engine is V8 15.0.245.2 (native155 SDK: 15.5). Engine builtins (Iterator.zip, Iterator.prototype.includes/join), error messages and ICU data follow the embedded V8 and are never spoofed. Closed by the harness/detection/engine re-version step.
CSS.supports answers from turbo-dom's real parser, which does not accept these Chrome 156 properties/functions yet. Faking `true` would contradict the computed style the same page can read.

Window own-property names native exposes and Chrome 156 does not: two absent-interface stub names from runtime.rs's stub list (PaintWorkletGlobalScope is worklet-only, webkitAudioContext was removed; StorageAccessHandle is no longer a global since turbo-surf#94) and one internal global (`__name`, the esbuild keepNames passthrough in runtime.rs; the hydration fetch drain counter `__pendingFetches` is private since turbo-surf#83). Pinned by name so any new extra global is a tell. Interface owners: API-INVENTORY.json / issue #28.
